requests.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: production RGBA reaction animation sprite sheet for the 2D Greek mythology roguelite Paradise in Hell.
Input image: identity, equipment, palette and rendering-style reference ONLY; do not copy its old row/column layout. Create NEW hurt and death animation drawings of the SAME enemy.
Canvas MUST be exactly1792x1280 pixels: an invisible grid of SEVEN columns and FIVE rows, each cell exactly256x256. Exactly35 complete sprites, one sprite in each cell. NO labels, text, numbers, visible grid, frames or background scene.
ROW DIRECTIONS, top to bottom: row0 DOWN/front (faces viewer); row1 UP/back (shows the back); row2 LEFT/strict side (nose and facing toward screen LEFT); row3 UP-LEFT (true diagonal rear-left, shows back plus left side); row4 DOWN-LEFT (true diagonal front-left, shows front plus left side). All seven cells in a row have the SAME facing. Do NOT draw any right-facing row. Diagonals must be authored three-quarter poses, not duplicate side views.
COLUMN ACTIONS, left to right: col0 HURT impact flinch; col1 HURT small backward recoil, body visibly cringing; col2 HURT recovery toward the original standing stance; col3 DEATH first loss of balance with knees bending; col4 DEATH dropping to one knee and tipping sideways; col5 DEATH falling almost horizontally toward the floor; col6 DEATH fully prone motionless body lying on its side. This is one continuous understandable fall in four drawings. Last death frame must show the FULL solid corpse and all its gear; no disappearing, dissolving, ghost, shrinking, fade, dismemberment or gore.
ANIMATION REGISTRATION: same character size and camera in every cell, standing height about200px with its feet/ground baseline at local y220, local body center x128. Preserve the same upright scale across ALL hurt and death frames: the corpse gets wider as it falls, never resized smaller or stretched to fill the cell. A horizontal corpse must be naturally wide and low and fit completely within its256px cell, with visible transparent gutter. Keep the ground baseline consistent at y220, avoid large position jumps or body teleportation. Only small recoil of torso/head, not a jump across the cell. No sprite or weapon may cross a cell edge. Keep skull/head, waist, limbs and equipment proportions coherent across poses and views.
Style: match the input image's readable hand-painted pixel-art game sprites, crisp dark contour and controlled textured shading, designed to downsample cleanly into64x64 game frames. Match the original anatomy, materials, outfit, hair/helmet and colors rather than redesigning the enemy. All carried equipment is part of the complete sprite, never a separate floating overlay.
Transparency: real alpha-zero empty background and gutters, no painted backdrop, checkerboard, floor ellipse or cast shadow. Preserve clean RGBA edges; no bright red/yellow/green chroma-key fringes, no edge garbage, no glowing halos, no colored matte. No added attack effects or impact stars, no blood splashes, no extra character.
SUBJECT: The COMMON GHOUL: the exact hunched grey-green undead man, short ragged dark hair, pale eyes, torn plum-purple one-shoulder tunic, brown wraps and boots, ONE bronze pauldron on his left shoulder (viewer RIGHT in the front view). Empty hands; no weapon.
